title: Add Synthetic RAG Chaos Grid Quickstart
author: Aditi Mehra
description:
Motivation: Teams building retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) features need a lightweight, reproducible playground to validate robustness of agent/tool-calling flows under realistic failure modes (latency spikes, transient errors, partial tool responses, hallucination injection). This quickstart introduces a self-contained 'Chaos Grid' that runs many small RAG sessions in parallel with configurable failure profiles so engineers can observe behavioral regressions, telemetry coverage, and recovery policies.

What this PR adds: a new quickstart under quickstarts/chaos-grid that provides: 1) a reproducible devcontainer and docker-compose sandbox to run a local Redwood-compatible HTTP shim and a set of stubbed tools (search, calculator, knowledgebase) that can be probabilistically faulty; 2) an orchestration harness (node + python runner) that executes parameterized RAG sessions across axes (tool-latency, tool-error-rate, index-staleness, response-corruption) and captures structured traces compatible with Redwood Console ingest; 3) a set of scenario templates (regression, canary, load, flaky-tools) and example promptsets designed to highlight common production failure classes; 4) docs and troubleshooting guidance including suggested Redwood Optimize settings and rollout policies to test.

Description (single continuous body): This PR implements a developer quickstart called "Synthetic RAG Chaos Grid" aimed at teams validating agent/tool-calling resiliency. The quickstart is intentionally sandboxed and does not require real upstream services or private data: all tools are stubbed and configurable via a single YAML file (.chaos/config.yaml). Users can vary failure profiles across an experiment grid and run a matrix of sessions that emit per-session traces (JSONL) and a summary CSV with key metrics (success-rate, mean-latency, tool-fallback-count, hallucination-score). Included are: a devcontainer.json for one-click VS Code onboarding, a docker-compose service that runs the local shim (redwood-proxy-mock), a lightweight node orchestrator (scripts/run-grid.js) and a small python evaluator (tools/score_hallucinations.py) used to approximate factual drift. The README explains how to run the four example scenarios, interpret traces in Redwood Console, and wire the output to CI (smoke/regression) using the provided runner flags.

Checklist: - [x] Add quickstart scaffolding and scenario templates - [x] Provide devcontainer and docker-compose for local reproducibility - [x] Add example promptsets and evaluation scorer - [x] Emit trace artifacts compatible with Console ingestion (span id, trace id, event tags) - [x] Add docs section on recommended Optimize parameters and rollout tests - [x] Add unit smoke CI for orchestration runner

Commit summary: commit 1: scaffold quickstart directory and README with runbook, commit 2: add devcontainer + docker-compose and redwood-proxy-mock, commit 3: implement node orchestration runner and YAML config parser, commit 4: add stubbed tools (search, calc, kb) with fault injection, commit 5: add python hallucination scorer and CSV summarizer, commit 6: docs + examples + small CI smoke test.

Files changed (high level): quickstarts/chaos-grid/README.md, quickstarts/chaos-grid/devcontainer.json, quickstarts/chaos-grid/docker-compose.yaml, quickstarts/chaos-grid/.chaos/config.example.yaml, quickstarts/chaos-grid/scripts/run-grid.js, quickstarts/chaos-grid/tools/stub_services.py, quickstarts/chaos-grid/tools/score_hallucinations.py, .github/workflows/chaos-grid-smoke.yml (adds a lightweight smoke CI). The diff is intentionally small per file with focused additions: example configs, orchestrator, and docs.

Testing and CI: The PR adds a workflow (chaos-grid-smoke) that boots a containerized shim and runs a single short grid with deterministic failure seeds to validate runner exit codes and artifact exports. CI passed on the final push after small lint fixes. Local dev tested in VS Code devcontainer on Linux and MacOS.

Review notes and risks: The quickstart includes a small HTTP shim (redwood-proxy-mock) that exposes a subset of Redwood API endpoints for local testing; it is explicitly documented and sandbox-only. No production credentials or secrets are included. The mock is not intended for performance benchmarking at scale; teams should migrate to dedicated Redwood Dedicated environments for throughput testing. The hallucination scorer is a heuristic and documented as such — we recommend pairing this quickstart with the team's eval harness for production-grade metrics.

How to try: follow README; example quick command: docker-compose up -d && devcontainer open . && node scripts/run-grid.js --scenario=canary --seed=42 --workers=4 --output=artifacts/seed-42.jsonl. The quickstart outputs artifacts that can be uploaded to Console using the documented ingestion script.

Related work: references to retrieval-authoring playgrounds and authoring devcontainer patterns (see ENG-1298 for rollout test definitions). This quickstart is intended as a developer-first complement to existing RAG examples by focusing on failure-mode exploration and CI-integration patterns.
